capabilities: Flag hidden files and folders with a count badge
Launch AI tools in the vault, project or git worktree folder
Sort notes into For me, For AI and Unsorted
Write all settings to a plain note
Require approval for changed commands and project links
disambiguation: Not an audience-analytics or publishing tool; it marks whether a note is written for a person or an AI.
extras: Desktop only; Windows support is new and untested. No network calls, accounts, API keys or telemetry. Commands, terminals and project links changed in the config note must be approved inside Obsidian before they run.
problem: Obsidian's file list leaves out scripts and data files, and notes carry no record of whether they are written for a person or an AI.

relations.evidence: One click opens a terminal and starts your AI tool (Claude Code, Codex, anything you type)
One click opens a terminal and starts your AI tool (Claude Code, Codex, anything you type)

requires.name: Terminal app (Terminal, iTerm2, Ghostty, WezTerm, Kitty, Alacritty, Rio, PowerShell, Windows Terminal)
AI command-line tool such as Claude Code or Codex

summary: Plugin for AI-workflow vaults that flags files Obsidian hides, launches AI tools in the right folder, and sorts notes by an audience property.
